text.guided:
Take the unit square: area **1**.
After a matrix, it becomes a parallelogram. Its area is the **determinant**.
With $\begin{bmatrix}3&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$, the square is 3 times wider: area 3.
text.fast: The unit square (area 1) becomes a parallelogram of area det(M). A 3× stretch gives area 3.

examples.games: Like a power-up that makes every sprite 3 times wider.
examples.physics: Like a gas expanding to 3 times its volume.
examples.ai: Like resizing an image: the number of pixels changes.

check.prompt: What is the new area of the unit square?

text.guided:
A shear slides the top of the square sideways.
The parallelogram leans, but its base and height do not change: the area stays **1**.
text.fast: Shears keep areas: det of $\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$ is 1.

examples.games: Like italic text: slanted, same amount of ink.
examples.physics: Like pushing the top of a deck of cards.
examples.ai: Like a skew augmentation: same pixels, slanted.

text.guided:
If the matrix turns the square **over** (like a mirror), the determinant is **negative**.
If it squashes the square into a line, the area is **0**: the plane is flattened.
text.fast: det < 0: the plane is flipped over. det = 0: everything is squashed onto a line.

examples.physics: Like looking at your hand in a mirror: left becomes right.
examples.ai: Like projecting 2D data onto a single line: information is lost.

scene.caption: Mirrored and twice as tall: area −2.
